parsed.attack: Kill line two states the failure outright: under $10 of lifetime revenue against a $20-80 cost per paying user. Run it - at the stated 15% of free-mock finishers buying, a $5.84 iOS install costs $39 per payer, plus the free 12-minute mocks burned on the 6.7 non-buyers behind each payer ($0.06-0.24 each at $0.005-0.02/minute), against $10-15 gross and $7-10.50 net from two small packs: 4-6x underwater. Naturalization is also a once-in-a-lifetime event, so there is no repeat purchase and no retention to amortise CAC against - every cohort is bought again from scratch, forever.
parsed.strongest_defence: The willingness-to-pay anchor in the idea is wrong, not the market's: against a $760 N-400 filing fee and $40/hour tutors, a $39-49 pack is trivial and nets $27-34 per payer; the audience skews Android ($1.92 CPI, so $12.80 per payer at 15% conversion), actively searches for interview prep so ASO installs are cheap, ESL classes and legal clinics are a zero-CAC institutional channel, and $0.06-0.24 of voice per mock leaves a 95% gross margin, not the 50-70% AI norm.
parsed.verdict_reason: The margin half is comfortably beaten and the audience has real willingness to pay, but the economics only close if the price rises 4-5x above the sub-$10 lifetime the kill line assumes and acquisition stays on Android CPIs or free institutional channels.
